newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH LENTEX CARPET MAKER SEEKS JANUARY IPO.
newsitem.headline: POLISH LENTEX CARPET MAKER SEEKS JANUARY IPO.

text.p: Polish carpet maker Zaklady Lentex SA has submitted an issue prospectus to the Securities Commission and seeks a January public offering, the firm's board chairman said on Friday.
Jan Wesolowski told Reuters that Lentex, in which National Investment Fund (NFI) No.1 has a strategic stake, could reach the Warsaw bourse's main market in the first quarter of 1997.
"We would like a January public offering at the latest ... and to reach the bourse in the first quarter of next year," Wesolowski said.

He said the firm, which currently has 4.5 million shares, would offer 1.4 million shares ex-rights in separate tranches for large and small investors and 100,000 shares in a tranche for employees and management.
He said large investors would be asked to provide a price through book-building.
Wesolowski said Lentex would invest at least 45 million zlotys over the next two years, about 60 percent of which would come from the issue and 40 percent from the firm's own funds.
He said the company had a 40-percent domestic market share in non-woven textiles.

Lentex, which employs 1,250 and whose full name was formerly Slaskie Zaklady Przemyslu Lniarskiego Lentex SA, made a net profit of 11.2 million zlotys last year and expects to earn 10 million this year on sales of 135 million zlotys.
NFI 1 currently holds 33 percent of the firm, the remaining 14 NFIs hold 27 percent, the state treasury 25 percent and employees 15 percent.
Under Poland's NFI mass privatisation programme each of Poland's 28 million adults can buy one NFI unit for 20 zlotys, later to be exchanged for shares in each of the 15 NFIs.
The funds group more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation and are run by foreign and domestic management firms.
